mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 12 months prior to the rate increase (t-test p > 0.05), or the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a rapid normalization of policy rates, causing a short-term spike in equity valuations and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in any high-inflation episode (p > 0.05), or the 2-month moving average of CPIAUCSL never exceeds 3% during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting equity market optimism and positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor market strengthening episodes (defined by PAYEMS/UNRATE thresholds), the 5-day forward return is not positive (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in GDPC1 (goods orders) of at least 5% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating business demand, which elevates earnings expectations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-over-month increase exceeds 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of similar demand expansion (GDPC1 MOM > 5% for 2 months), 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 30-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 4% in a month coincides with a decline in RSAFS (retail sales) by over 2%, signaling weak demand-side pressures that depress equity valuations and drive negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 4% in a single month AND RSAFS falls by > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: In 50% of historical supply contraction episodes (defined by INDPRO/RSAFS thresholds), the 60-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the expectation of future rate cuts supports risk asset valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During all 12 months where FEDFUNDS was below 2% for 3 months, the 20-day forward return was not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in HOUST (housing starts) by 10% in a month while UNRATE remains below 4% suggests a potential housing market correction that weighs on consumer confidence and equity prices, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 10% in a single month AND UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: In 70% of historical housing corrections (HOUST drop >10% with UNRATE <4%), the 5-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in the 12-month moving average of INDPRO (industrial production) while CPIAUCSL shows no acceleration suggests a softening in supply chain activity without price pressures, which can lead to cautious investor behavior and negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 12-month MA of INDPRO declines for 2 consecutive months AND 12-month MA of CPIAUCSL does not accelerate (monthly change
failure_condition: During 40% of historical supply softening episodes (as defined), the 60-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.4).
